title: CoC 7e Investigator
description: Source-of-truth record for a pregen investigator or a mechanically-full elite NPC. Field model follows a full 7e character sheet, not just the stat block. See core/13-create-investigator.md and reference/rules/character-creation.md. Only name/occupation/characteristics/derived/skills are required — a thin elite-NPC record stays legal.

player.description: Who is playing them. Omit for elite NPCs.

occupation_detail.description: The occupation's mechanical contract. Record it so the point ledger can be audited without reopening the rulebook.

skill_points_formula.description: e.g. "EDU x 4" or "EDU x 2 + DEX x 2".

occupation_skills.description: The occupation's own skill list, including any free-choice slots ("any one other skill").

contacts.description: Typical professional contacts — a ready-made hook source.

era_year.description: In-fiction year. Gates period-appropriate skills, gear, and weapons.

characteristics.description: Final values after age modifiers. Halves and fifths are derived at the table, never stored.

age_modifiers.description: What the age band actually cost. Recorded so a reviewer can re-derive the final characteristics from the rolls.

physical_deduction.description: Total points removed across STR/CON/DEX (or STR/SIZ for 15-19).

deduction_split.description: How that total was split, e.g. "STR -3, CON -2".

edu_gained.description: Points actually gained from those checks.

luck_rolls.description: 15-19 rolls Luck twice and keeps the better.

major_wound.description: Half of maximum HP, rounded down.

Luck.description: Rolled 3D6 x 5, not derived from anything.

Dodge.description: Starts at DEX / 2; may be raised with skill points like any other skill.

Armor.description: Worn armour and the points it stops. Omit or "none" for most investigators.

currency.description: e.g. "USD 1920s". Cash and assets are era-scaled — see reference/rules/character-creation.md.

assets.description: Value of everything not immediately spendable.

spending_level.description: What they can spend casually without accounting for it.

asset_notes.description: What the assets actually are — property, vehicle, holdings.

skill_points.description: The point ledger. If spent does not equal total, the sheet is wrong.

cap.description: Any table-declared cap, e.g. "occupation 70 / interest 60". Default is the rulebook's 90.

specialization.description: For the umbrella skills — Art/Craft, Science, Survival, Fighting, Firearms, Pilot, Language, Lore. The generic parent is never bought on its own. Put the family in `name` and the specific here; do not repeat it inside `name`.

base.description: The skill's starting value before any points.

value.description: Final percentage. Must equal base + occupation + interest + growth.

occupation_skill.description: True if it is on the occupation's list — the only skills occupation points may buy.

checked.description: Carries a growth check mark from play.

skill.description: The skill it is rolled against, e.g. "Fighting (Brawl)".

gear.description: Carried equipment. Keep it to what the scenario can actually use.

experience_packages.description: Optional pre-play history (a war, a beat, a stretch inside, a Mythos brush) bought with starting Sanity. Each one buys a mechanical edge and mandates a matching backstory entry — see reference/rules/character-creation.md.

requires.description: Constraints it imposes — minimum age, a mandatory scar/phobia backstory entry.

mythos_encounters.description: What they have already met and what it cost. Elite NPCs and veteran pregens only.

backstory.description: The 7e backstory prompts. Fill every one, then cut what the campaign cannot use.

backstory_keys.description: Which backstory entries are marked KEY — the ones tied hardest to who they are. Values are backstory field names. A key entry restores Sanity when its bond is honoured, and is lost for good when the bond breaks.

status.description: Live condition. Starts clean on a fresh pregen; tracked by core/12-canon-update.md thereafter.

physical.description: e.g. healthy, wounded, major wound, unconscious, dying.

mental.description: e.g. sane, temporary insanity, indefinite insanity, permanently insane.

party.description: Fellow investigators and how they know each other — the cheapest way to make a one-shot party cohere.

growth_log.description: What play changed, newest last. Append only.

hooks.description: Each hook must tie into something the campaign can actually use — an NPC, faction, location, or the central mystery.
